source.title: Accelerated High-Accuracy Sampling from a Warm Start via the Proximal Bouncy Particle Sampler

domains.carrier: Authors source is R^d. A future finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel realization, including rank zero, is an explicitly labelled generalization, not an added restriction.
domains.parameters: V:E->R; alpha,beta nonnegative reals; eta real; fixed deterministic y,r,z0 and n in Nat. No random event depth or physical-time stopping index.
domains.phase: z=(x,p) in E x E. c=y-eta gradV(r), g_r(x)=gradV(x)-gradV(r), literal harmonic Phi, reflection S with R0=I, and lambda=sqrt(eta)*max(0,<p,g_r(x)>).
domains.hazard: Lambda_z(s)=integral_0^s lambda(Phi_t z)dt; tau_z(e)=inf{s>=0:Lambda_z(s)>=e} in [0,infinity], inf empty=infinity.
domains.history: D=([0,infinity) x (E x E)) + {stopped}; R0=live(0,z0), R_(k+1) uses zero-based threshold k, infinity causes stopped and stopped remains absorbing. H_n=(R0,...,Rn) in D^(Fin(n+1)). All abstract histories allowed in measurable kernel assertions.
domains.clock_model: P=product_k Exp1 on raw R^Nat; epsilon_k=max(w_k,0) is the declared ambient null-set extension. H_n consumes k<n; full raw Y_n(w)_k=w_(n+k) is independent of H_n. Source E_(n+1) is raw w_n.
domains.time_measure: Use positive finite s in NNReal with canonical Lebesgue trace nu: pushforward of real Lebesgue restricted to [0,infinity) under t->max(t,0). Hence nu({0})=0 and nu((a,b])=b-a for 0<=a<=b. Equivalent real-time notation on (0,infinity) is acceptable only with the exact restriction/coercion identity, never a rescaled or arbitrary measure.

admissible_test_class.A: Any Borel A subset of Hist_n; no positive history-law mass requirement.
admissible_test_class.d: Every fixed deterministic Borel map d:Hist_n->NNReal. Each d(h) is finite, but d need not be bounded across histories. d(H_n) can be random. There is no omega/tail argument and no external random function d.
admissible_test_class.F: Every jointly Borel nonnegative extended test F:Hist_n x NNReal -> ENNReal, including indicator tests of arbitrary Borel joint history/time sets. Nonnegative extended tests require no integrability provider; results may be infinity. A bounded real signed test is a later corollary requiring its internally derived integrability, not an extra standing source hypothesis.
admissible_test_class.classification: Source-implicit admissible measurable test interface, not pure typing and not seventh/eighth analytic premises. Joint measurability cannot be replaced by separately measurable sections alone.
admissible_test_class.tail_restriction: F and d inspect only the complete deterministic-depth history and a supplied prospective finite time s. They cannot inspect the unused threshold or future input sequence.
admissible_test_class.constructor: On a live last record (T,z) and positive finite prospective wait s, the prescribed next record is live(T+s,S(Phi_s z)); appending it to h is the finite next-history constructor. Its joint Borel property is derived from A.2 maps and finite-product/tag operations. Stopped histories have no next phase; the finite-density measure is zero there. Future F may compose with this Borel constructor to represent actual ordered-time integrands without a constructor-law provider.

source_implicit_target.parent_global_boundary: G86-11 / density component of S87-I5 only
source_implicit_target.density: rho(h,s)=lambda(Phi_s z)*exp(-Lambda_z(s)) when h_last=live(T,z); rho(h,s)=0 when h_last=stopped, for finite s>=0.
source_implicit_target.kernel: K_d(h,C)=integral_{0<s<d(h)} 1_C(s) rho(h,s) nu(ds). Joint-set form uses 1_B(h,s), B Borel in Hist_n x NNReal. K_d is a Borel subprobability kernel on the entire abstract history space.
source_implicit_target.strict_joint_test_identity: For all Borel A, d and jointly Borel nonnegative F: integral J_(A,d,F)(w) P(dw) = integral_{h in A} integral_{0<s<d(h)} F(h,s) rho(h,s) nu(ds) mu_n(dh), where mu_n=(H_n)_*P.
source_implicit_target.actual_observable: J is F(H_n(w),s) only on H_n(w) in A, last record live(T,z), and tau_z(epsilon_n(w))=s with 0<s<d(H_n(w)); otherwise J=0. The guard forces the waiting time finite. Any total finite extraction or zero outside this guard is an observable encoding, never a fictitious stopped/infinite wait or state.
source_implicit_target.equivalent_measure_form: Equality of the strict finite joint-history/wait submeasure with 1_(0<s<d(h))*rho(h,s) times mu_n(dh)nu(ds). This measure equality for every Borel joint set is equivalent to the nonnegative joint-test formulation by nonnegative integration.
required_measurability: rho is jointly Borel and pointwise finite/nonnegative on all histories and finite times
the guarded actual-clock joint test/event is measurable
h->integral_(0,d(h)) F(h,s)rho(h,s)nu(ds) is measurable for every admissible joint F
h->K_d(h,C) is measurable for every Borel C
source_implicit_target.required_finiteness: For every history h, K_d(h,whole)<=1, so K_d is a finite subprobability kernel. The resulting joint measure on A has mass<=mu_n(A)<=1. rho itself need not be bounded by1; for arbitrary unbounded F the weighted integral need not be finite.
source_implicit_target.publication_attribution: This is an ASTIS source-implicit completion of the finite next-event density needed when the authors iterate independent threshold factors in A.7; it is not a separately printed author theorem.

endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.existing_finite_density_convention: The accepted deterministic-state finite first-event producer uses 0<tau<=T and a density measure restricted to Ioc(0,T). This source ingredient is reused mathematically; no89 Lean candidate or producer implementation was inspected to choose the topology.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.strict_route: For each fixed history h and t=d(h), restrict that measure equality further to Iio(t). Both sides become Ioo(0,t), with arbitrary Borel section/test retained. Restricting an equality of measures is exact and requires no claim that Ioc and Ioo have equal total mass.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.no_atom_distinction: No finite-atom lemma is an AND parent for this strict restricted density/subprobability target. If a later statement equates <= and < cutoff event probabilities, or asserts strict mass=1-exp(-Lambda(t)) using an existing closed-cutoff mass formula, it must internally derive zero mass at the finite boundary from the density (and tau=0 null from positive exponential clocks). Such a lemma may not be supplied as a public provider premise.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.assessment_history: An initial source-review scheduling message treated a no-finite-atom bridge as mandatory for the strict density route. Before any candidate existed, abstract measure restriction was independently checked: the bridge is needed for endpoint-mass equivalence, not for restricting both sides to a strict set. This freeze records the corrected smaller route without silently retaining a false AND.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.zero_duration: d(h)=0 makes the strict finite interval empty and K_d=0. No positive cutoff premise.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.zero_threshold: tau_z(0)=0; strict positive finite guard excludes it. Raw nonpositive thresholds lie in the explicitly declared P-null extension.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.finite_endpoint: Exactly tau=d(h) is excluded on both actual and reference sides by restriction, not ignored by an unproved no-atom assertion.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.live_infinity: Live states with tau=infinity contribute zero to the finite density measure. Their no-event survival mass remains in the extended wait law and is not discarded or renormalized.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.stopped: Already stopped records contribute the zero finite kernel and zero actual test. No next waiting time/state is assigned physical meaning.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.zero_hazard: A zero rate along the whole orbit gives rho=0 and no positive finite waits; mass can be0. Initial instantaneous rate0 alone does not imply a zero orbit hazard.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.null_A: If mu_n(A)=0, the joint finite submeasure and both test integrals vanish, even for nonnegative extended F. No conditional point-division is used.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.n_zero: H0 is the deterministic live(0,z0) history and w0 is fresh; the identity reduces to the deterministic-state strict finite density with a fixed section/test.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.rank_zero: In a finite-dimensional generalization of rank0, rate/hazard/density are0. H0 is live with infinite next wait P-a.s.; later records are stopped. All finite density/subprobability claims give0.
endpoint_and_degenerate_conventions.unrealizable_histories: rho, K_d and their Borel/subprobability assertions hold for every abstract history using its last tag/state; actual law only weights realizable histories through mu_n.

source_author_vs_ASTIS: Authors print the iid threshold construction, finite updates/stopping and A.7 iteration over strict ordered times; A.2 prints joint Borel recursion. The deterministic finite density and complete-history product substrate are previously verified ASTIS completions. The proposed random-history finite density/joint-test integration is another attributed ASTIS completion, not a printed standalone author result.
necessary_internal_derivation: Joint Borel/nonnegative rho and measurable cutoff/test/finite-clock observable on whole carriers
At fixed h, restrict the existing deterministic Ioc density measure law by Iio(d(h)) and evaluate the Borel section
Integrate these pointwise sections using actual H_n/full raw-tail product law and Tonelli/nonnegative integration
Derive kernel mass<=1 and joint measure mass<=mu_n(A), retaining stopped0 and missing infinite-wait mass
provider_binders_forbidden: unused-clock independence or joint product law
no-atom or positive conditioning-event mass certificates

consumer.real_source_use: Each jump factor lambda(pre-bounce state) exp(-integrated arc hazard) in A.7; multiplying through actual finite history and prospective next time requires joint history/time tests.
consumer.ordered_time_cutoff: For fixed horizon T, the Borel choice d_T(h)=max(T-last_live_time,0), stopped0, with live last_time<T in the history event, imposes the next strict ordered event time<T.
consumer.next_state: F(h,s) may compose with the jointly Borel finite constructor live(last_time+s,S(Phi_s last_state)) and finite appended history; no actual next-state theorem is silently assumed.
consumer.unclosed: Density does not alone supply conditional iteration/disintegration, final survival assembly, prescribed path functional, count partition/sum convergence, or full A.7.
